claim.pdf_says: In all three DIVIDE figures the exception rows print as 'ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1' / 'NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2' where SIZE and ERROR carry underline rules and NOT carries an underline rule, but ON is NOT underlined in either row (verified on the enlarged crop of the Format 1 block).
claim.markdown_says: > **Figure notes (DIVIDE Format 1 (into) syntax diagram).** `DIVIDE`, `INTO`, `ON`, `SIZE`, `ERROR`, `NOT`, and `END-DIVIDE` are underlined in the printed standard (required words).  -- and identically in the Format 2 note ('`DIVIDE`, `INTO`, `GIVING`, `ON`, `SIZE`, `ERROR`, `NOT`, and `END-DIVIDE`') and the Format 3 note ('`DIVIDE`, `BY`, `GIVING`, `ON`, `SIZE`, `ERROR`, `NOT`, and `END-DIVIDE`')
claim.why_it_matters: ON is an optional word in the ON SIZE ERROR phrase -- 'SIZE ERROR ...' and 'NOT SIZE ERROR ...' are legal COBOL. Three figure notes on this page assert ON is a required word, which is the transcription's own annotation contradicting the printed glyphs and would drive an implementation to reject legal source. The correctly-written sibling notes on pages 618, 619 and 640 list only the genuinely underlined words and omit ON.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on independent inspection of the rendered page and by pixel measurement; the claim is accurate as written and if anything understates its own evidence.

WHAT THE PRINTED GLYPHS SHOW. Rendered specs/ISO_COBOL PDF page 644 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v644/spec_p644.png, 2550x3300) and cropped each exception block at 3x. Visually, in every one of the three DIVIDE formats the exception rows read 'ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1' over 'NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2', and in both rows SIZE, ERROR and NOT sit on visible underline rules while ON sits on bare white space -- the gap in the rule is plainly visible between the end of NOT's rule and the start of SIZE's rule.

I did not stop at the eyeball. I segmented each row into word clusters by column-darkness and computed, for each cluster, the fraction of its horizontal extent covered by dark pixels in the underline band a few pixels below the baseline. All six exception rows on the page:
  Format 1 row 1 (y~1253 rule): ON x=381-434 coverage 0.00 | SIZE x=453-533 coverage 0.95 | ERROR x=555-689 coverage 0.96 | imperative-statement-1 coverage 0.00
  Format 1 row 2 (y~1325 rule): NOT x=380-461 coverage 0.94 | ON x=479-532 coverage 0.00 | SIZE 0.97 | ERROR 0.98 | imperative-statement-2 0.00
  Format 2 row 1 (y~1974 rule): ON 0.00 | SIZE 0.95 | ERROR 0.96
  Format 2 row 2 (y~2046 rule): NOT 0.94 | ON 0.00 | SIZE 0.97 | ERROR 0.98
  Format 3 row 1 (y~2676 rule): ON 0.00 | SIZE 0.95 | ERROR 0.96
  Format 3 row 2 (y~2748 rule): NOT 0.94 | ON 0.00 | SIZE 0.95 | ERROR 0.97
Zero coverage under ON in all six occurrences, against 0.94-0.98 for every genuinely underlined word on the same rule row. This is not a faint or dropped rule: there is no ink at all beneath ON. The underline rules for DIVIDE, INTO, BY, GIVING and END-DIVIDE elsewhere on the page are present, so the page did not render with underlines suppressed.

WHAT THE TRANSCRIPTION SAYS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26640-26641, 26661-26662 and 26681-26682 (page-644 block starts at line 26612) carry the three figure notes exactly as quoted in the claim, each listing `ON` inside the enumeration terminated by 'are underlined in the printed standard (required words)'. The claim quotes all three verbatim; no misquotation. Note these blockquote figure notes are the transcription's OWN editorial annotation, not printed text -- so this is an annotation that fabricates a normative property the source does not have, which is worse than a lossy transcription of printed text.

WHY IT IS NORMATIVE, NOT COSMETIC. The spec defines the convention itself, and the transcription preserves it: §5.2.2 Keywords -- 'They are shown in uppercase and underlined in general formats. They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword'; §5.2.3 Optional words -- 'They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats. They may be written to add clarity.' ON printed without a rule is therefore an OPTIONAL word by the standard's own stated convention, so `DIVIDE A INTO B SIZE ERROR ...` and `... NOT SIZE ERROR ...` are legal COBOL. An implementer reading these three notes and taking them at face value would gate the SIZE ERROR phrase on a mandatory ON token and reject conforming source -- the precise 'reject legal source' failure mode the claim names.

THE SIBLING-NOTE CORROBORATION CHECKS OUT. I pulled the notes the claim cites. Page 618 (CALL): 'Underlined (required) words: CALL, REFERENCE, CONTENT, USING, RETURNING, EXCEPTION, NOT, END-CALL.' Page 619 (CALL Format 2): 'Required words (underlined in the printed figure): CALL, AS, NESTED, REFERENCE, CONTENT, VALUE, OMITTED, USING, RETURNING, EXCEPTION, NOT, END-CALL.' Page 640 (DISPLAY): 'Underlined required words: DISPLAY, LINE, COLUMN, COL, EXCEPTION, NOT, END-DISPLAY.' All three transcribe the structurally identical `ON EXCEPTION` / `NOT ON EXCEPTION` bracket-with-choice-indicators group and all three correctly omit ON. Page 644 is the outlier, which makes this a transcription defect rather than a house convention.

REFUTATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED. (a) 'The text is present, just reflowed' -- inapplicable; the defect is an extra false assertion, not missing text. (b) 'The fenced code blocks lost it' -- the code blocks are innocent; plain text cannot carry underlines and they correctly spell out ON SIZE ERROR. Only the annotation is wrong. (c) 'Maybe the note means words appearing in uppercase, not underlined ones' -- ruled out by the note's own literal wording, 'are underlined in the printed standard (required words)', which is a direct factual claim about the glyphs. (d) 'Maybe ON is required specifically after NOT' -- ruled out by measurement: in the NOT row NOT scores 0.94 and the immediately adjacent ON scores 0.00 on the same rule row. (e) 'Render artifact' -- ruled out by the 0.94-0.98 vs 0.00 separation and by underlines rendering correctly everywhere else on the page.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed and accurately described; scope is slightly broader than the claim's stated verification. The claim verified Format 1 by eye; I verified ALL SIX exception rows (both rows in each of Formats 1, 2 and 3) both visually at 3x and by pixel-coverage measurement of the underline band. In every row ON has exactly 0.00 underline coverage while NOT, SIZE and ERROR score 0.94-0.98. Per the standard's own conventions -- §5.2.2 (keywords are underlined and required) and §5.2.3 (optional words are uppercase and not underlined) -- ON is an OPTIONAL word of the SIZE ERROR phrase, so `SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1` and `NOT SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2` are conforming. The defect is confined to the transcription's own editorial 'Figure notes' blockquotes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26640-26641 (Format 1), 26661-26662 (Format 2) and 26681-26682 (Format 3); the fenced general-format blocks themselves are correct. Fix: delete `ON` from the required-word enumeration in all three notes, leaving Format 1 as DIVIDE, INTO, SIZE, ERROR, NOT, END-DIVIDE; Format 2 as DIVIDE, INTO, GIVING, SIZE, ERROR, NOT, END-DIVIDE; Format 3 as DIVIDE, BY, GIVING, SIZE, ERROR, NOT, END-DIVIDE -- matching the correctly-written sibling notes on pages 618, 619 and 640, which I confirmed all omit ON for the structurally identical ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION group. Worth sweeping every other figure note in the transcription that enumerates required words for an ON-introduced conditional phrase (ON SIZE ERROR, ON EXCEPTION, ON OVERFLOW, AT END, INVALID KEY), since the same annotation error is likely to recur on the ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY and COMPUTE pages.
